question: Assume today is 2026-09-06. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park in September 2026, as it will be reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics.

target.what: Number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park during the full calendar month of September 2026, as reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics (Visitor Use Statistics), not unique visitors and not a year-to-date total.
target.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), U.S. Department of the Interior
target.cadence: Monthly, with preliminary monthly figures and year-to-date tables generally released after the month ends; revisions possible.
target.caveats: The target month is future/ongoing as of the 2026-09-06 cutoff (only September 1-6 have elapsed), so the estimate is a forecast. NPS 'recreation visits' are counted visits/entries, not unique people. September 2026 includes Labor Day on September 7 and school-start effects. Scheduled road closures,

candidates.perspective: NPS visitor-use statistician using long-run monthly tables
candidates.hypothesis: Yellowstone September visitation has a stable seasonal relationship to adjacent months and annual totals; the 2026 September value can be estimated as V_Sep2026 = V_Sep2025 × current-year growth factor, or as a September share of the 2026 annual/YTD level. Prior September values and the latest 2026 published YTD values anchor the baseline.

assumptions.name: Ratio of Yellowstone September recreation visits to the same year's July recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: No September park-total observation exists in the kept evidence, so the seasonal shape must be supplied. September is a shoulder month in Yellowstone: it retains the post-Labor-Day family travel tail but loses most school-age travel, so it typically runs somewhat above two-thirds of the July peak. The range is deliberately wide (P10-P90) to cover a cool/smoky September (near 0.55) and a warm, late- Labor-Day year (near 0.85), and to absorb the fact that this ratio is inferred from general park seasonality rather than from a retrieved series.
assumptions.applies_when: July 2026 (p1) is a valid same-year anchor for the September level, i.e. no large demand or access shift occurs between July and September 2026 beyond normal seasonality.
assumptions.falsified_by: Retrieved September park totals for recent years showing a September/July ratio persistently outside roughly 0.55-0.85 (e.g. the 2021 record shoulder season), or a September 2026 closure that removes access at a major gate.

assumptions.name: September share of Yellowstone annual recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: Used to convert an annual level into a September level because the collected evidence contains annual and year-to-date totals but no monthly September value. Recent Yellowstone years distribute roughly 14-15% of annual visits into September (the month follows the July-August peak of about 20% each). The range allows for a weak shoulder month (~11.5%) and a strong one (~18.5%); it also has to absorb the upward bias created by the autumn 2025 shutdown (p24), which depressed the late-2025 months and therefore inflates September's share of the 2025 annual total (p11).
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 annual total is close to the 2025 level after the year-to-date growth adjustment (p5/p6), so September 2026 inherits a normal seasonal share.
assumptions.falsified_by: A retrieved September value for any recent year implying a September share well below 0.115 or well above 0.185 of that year's annual total.

assumptions.name: Factor by which the September park-total-to-South-Entrance ratio departs from the annual ratio
assumptions.rationale: The annual park/South ratio (p11/p59) is dominated by midsummer, when park-wide traffic peaks. South Entrance holds up better in the shoulder season because Jackson/Grand Teton-based travel continues after the family-summer peak: South Entrance's own September count (p58) exceeds 80% of its July count (p61), whereas park-wide September is typically nearer 65-75% of July. Hence the September park/South ratio should sit below the annual ratio, around 0.8, with a wide range because the park-wide September figure is unobserved.
assumptions.applies_when: South Entrance remains open and uncongested through September 2026 and its shoulder-season composition (Grand Teton/Jackson flows) is unchanged from 2025.
assumptions.falsified_by: Gate-level September data showing South Entrance's share of park totals in September equal to or below its annual share (factor near or above 1.0), or a South Entrance closure/reopening change in 2026.

assumptions.name: Departure factor of the 2026 September-to-July recreation-visit ratio from the observed 2021 September-to-July ratio
assumptions.rationale: The 2021 pair p103 and p3 fixes one observed same-year September/July ratio (roughly four-fifths). September levels have since held up much better than July: p101 (September 2024) is only a little below p103 (September 2021), while p1 (July 2026) is about a tenth below p3 (July 2021). Because July 2026 is relatively depressed, the 2026 September/July ratio should sit above the 2021 ratio, so the departure factor is placed modestly above 1 with a range reaching back to 1 (no change) and up to about a fifth higher for a mild shoulder season.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 has a shoulder-season shape broadly like recent Yellowstone years, with no major September road closure, reservation change, or heavy smoke episode.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published September 2026 total implying a September/July ratio at or below the 2021 ratio, or evidence of a major September closure or smoke event cutting park access.

assumptions.name: Departure factor of the 2026 September share of annual recreation visits from the mean observed September share in 2021, 2023 and 2024
assumptions.rationale: The three observed September totals divided by their own-year annual totals (p101/p13, p102/p14, p103/p12) cluster tightly near one-fifth, with no trend, so the historical mean is a good center for 2026. residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.

The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
